member.summary: Gets or sets the implicit wait timeout, which is the amount of time the driver should wait when searching for an element if it is not immediately present.
member.remarks:
When searching for a single element, the driver should poll the page until the element has been found, or this timeout expires before throwing a . When searching for multiple elements, the driver should poll the page until at least one element has been found or this timeout has expired.
Increasing the implicit wait timeout should be used judiciously as it will have an adverse effect on test run time, especially when used with slower location strategies like XPath.

member.summary: Gets or sets the implicit wait timeout, which is the amount of time the driver should wait when searching for an element if it is not immediately present.
member.remarks:
When searching for a single element, the driver should poll the page until the element has been found, or this timeout expires before throwing a . When searching for multiple elements, the driver should poll the page until at least one element has been found or this timeout has expired.
Increasing the implicit wait timeout should be used judiciously as it will have an adverse effect on test run time, especially when used with slower location strategies like XPath.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.IWebDriver
member.summary: Defines the interface through which the user controls the browser.
member.remarks:
The interface is the main interface to use for testing, which represents an idealized web browser. The methods in this class fall into three categories:
Control of the browser itself
Selection of IWebElements
Debugging aids
Key properties and methods are , which is used to load a new web page by setting the property, and the various methods similar to , which is used to find IWebElements.
You use the interface by instantiate drivers that implement of this interface. You should write your tests against this interface so that you may "swap in" a more fully featured browser when there is a requirement for one.

member.remarks: Setting the property will load a new web page in the current browser window. This is done using an HTTP GET operation, and the method will block until the load is complete. This will follow redirects issued either by the server or as a meta-redirect from within the returned HTML. Should a meta-redirect "rest" for any duration of time, it is best to wait until this timeout is over, since should the underlying page change while your test is executing the results of future calls against this interface will be against the freshly loaded page.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.IWebDriver.PageSource
member.summary: Gets the source of the page last loaded by the browser.
member.remarks: If the page has been modified after loading (for example, by JavaScript) there is no guarantee that the returned text is that of the modified page. Please consult the documentation of the particular driver being used to determine whether the returned text reflects the current state of the page or the text last sent by the web server. The page source returned is a representation of the underlying DOM: do not expect it to be formatted or escaped in the same way as the response sent from the web server.

member.summary: Gets or sets the normalized pressure of the pointer input.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.Interactions.PointerInputDevice.PointerEventProperties.TangentialPressure
member.summary: Gets or sets the normalized tangential pressure (also known as barrel pressure) of the pointer input.
member.remarks: Valid values are between -1 and 1 with 0 being the neutral position of the control. Some hardware may only support positive values between 0 and 1.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.Interactions.PointerInputDevice.PointerEventProperties.TiltX
member.summary: Gets or sets the plane angle in degrees between the Y-Z plane and the plane containing both the transducer (e.g. pen stylus) axis and the Y axis..
member.remarks: Valid values are between -90 and 90. A positive value is to the right.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.Interactions.PointerInputDevice.PointerEventProperties.TiltY
member.summary: Gets or sets the plane angle in degrees between the X-Z plane and the plane containing both the transducer (e.g. pen stylus) axis and the X axis..
member.remarks: Valid values are between -90 and 90. A positive value is toward the user.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.Interactions.PointerInputDevice.PointerEventProperties.Twist
member.summary: Gets or sets the clockwise rotation in degrees of a transducer (e.g. stylus) around its own major axis
member.remarks: Valid values are between 0 and 359.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.Interactions.PointerInputDevice.PointerEventProperties.AltitudeAngle
member.summary: Gets or sets the altitude in radians of the transducer (e.g. pen/stylus)
member.remarks: Valid values are between 0 and π/2, where 0 is parallel to the surface (X-Y plane), and π/2 is perpendicular to the surface.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.Interactions.PointerInputDevice.PointerEventProperties.AzimuthAngle
member.summary: Gets or sets the azimuth angle (in radians) of the transducer (e.g. pen/stylus)
member.remarks: Valid values are between 0 and 2π, where 0 represents a transducer whose cap is pointing in the direction of increasing X values, and the values progressively increase when going clockwise.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.Manager.SeleniumManager
member.summary: Manages automatic discovery and configuration of browser drivers.
member.remarks:
Warning: This is an experimental API that is subject to change in future versions.
Selenium Manager automatically locates or downloads the appropriate browser driver for the specified browser. It eliminates the need for manual driver management by:
Detecting the installed browser version
Downloading the matching driver binary if needed
Caching drivers for subsequent use
Providing paths to both driver and browser executables
The Selenium Manager binary is automatically included with the Selenium package. Set the SE_MANAGER_PATH environment variable to use a custom binary location.

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.Manager.SeleniumManager.DiscoverBrowserAsync(System.String,OpenQA.Selenium.Manager.BrowserDiscoveryOptions,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Discovers the browser and driver paths for the specified browser.
member.param: The name of the browser (e.g., "chrome", "firefox", "edge").
Optional discovery options to control browser and driver resolution.
A token to cancel the asynchronous operation. When cancellation is requested, the Selenium Manager process is terminated.
member.returns: A representing the asynchronous operation, containing a with the paths to the driver and browser executables.
member.exception: Thrown when is null, empty, or whitespace.
Thrown when Selenium Manager fails to locate or download the required binaries.
Thrown when the operation is canceled via .

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.Timeouts.ImplicitWait
member.summary: Gets or sets the implicit wait timeout, which is the amount of time the driver should wait when searching for an element if it is not immediately present.
member.remarks:
When searching for a single element, the driver should poll the page until the element has been found, or this timeout expires before throwing a . When searching for multiple elements, the driver should poll the page until at least one element has been found or this timeout has expired.
Increasing the implicit wait timeout should be used judiciously as it will have an adverse effect on test run time, especially when used with slower location strategies like XPath.
Also can be managed via driver option.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.Timeouts.AsynchronousJavaScript
member.summary: Gets or sets the asynchronous script timeout, which is the amount of time the driver should wait when executing JavaScript asynchronously. This timeout only affects the method.

remarks.para: Also can be managed via driver option.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.Timeouts.PageLoad
member.summary: Gets or sets the page load timeout, which is the amount of time the driver should wait for a page to load when setting the property.

remarks.para: Also can be managed via driver option.

member.summary: Query a DOM node's accessibility subtree for accessible name and role. This command computes the name and role for all nodes in the subtree, including those that are ignored for accessibility, and returns those that match the specified name and role. member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Autofill.AddressUI
member.summary: Defines how an address can be displayed like in chrome://settings/addresses. Address UI is a two dimensional array, each inner array is an "address information line", and when rendered in a UI surface should be displayed as such. The following address UI for instance: [[{name: "GIVE_NAME", value: "Jon"}, {name: "FAMILY_NAME", value: "Doe"}], [{name: "CITY", value: "Munich"}, {name: "ZIP", value: "81456"}]] should allow the receiver to render: Jon Doe Munich 81456

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.CSS.CSSAdapter.ResolveValues(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.CSS.ResolveValuesCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Resolve the specified values in the context of the provided element. For example, a value of '1em' is evaluated according to the computed 'font-size' of the element and a value 'calc(1px + 2px)' will be resolved to '3px'. If the `propertyName` was specified the `values` are resolved as if they were property's declaration. If a value cannot be parsed according to the provided property syntax, the value is parsed using combined syntax as if null `propertyName` was provided. If the value cannot be resolved even then, return the provided value without any changes. Note: this function currently does not resolve CSS random() function, it returns unmodified random() function parts.`

member.summary: Starts tracking the given node for the computed style updates and whenever the computed style is updated for node, it queues a `computedStyleUpdated` event with throttling. There can only be 1 node tracked for computed style updates so passing a new node id removes tracking from the previous node. Pass `undefined` to disable tracking.

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.CSS.CSSAdapter.TrackComputedStyleUpdates(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.CSS.TrackComputedStyleUpdatesCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Starts tracking the given computed styles for updates. The specified array of properties replaces the one previously specified. Pass empty array to disable tracking. Use takeComputedStyleUpdates to retrieve the list of nodes that had properties modified. The changes to computed style properties are only tracked for nodes pushed to the front-end by the DOM agent. If no changes to the tracked properties occur after the node has been pushed to the front-end, no updates will be issued for the node.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.CSS.ResolveValuesCommandSettings
member.summary: Resolve the specified values in the context of the provided element. For example, a value of '1em' is evaluated according to the computed 'font-size' of the element and a value 'calc(1px + 2px)' will be resolved to '3px'. If the `propertyName` was specified the `values` are resolved as if they were property's declaration. If a value cannot be parsed according to the provided property syntax, the value is parsed using combined syntax as if null `propertyName` was provided. If the value cannot be resolved even then, return the provided value without any changes. Note: this function currently does not resolve CSS random() function, it returns unmodified random() function parts.`

member.summary: Starts tracking the given computed styles for updates. The specified array of properties replaces the one previously specified. Pass empty array to disable tracking. Use takeComputedStyleUpdates to retrieve the list of nodes that had properties modified. The changes to computed style properties are only tracked for nodes pushed to the front-end by the DOM agent. member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Debugger.DebuggerAdapter.RestartFrame(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary:
Restarts particular call frame from the beginning. The old, deprecated behavior of `restartFrame` is to stay paused and allow further CDP commands after a restart was scheduled. This can cause problems with restarting, so we now continue execution immediatly after it has been scheduled until we reach the beginning of the restarted frame.
To stay back-wards compatible, `restartFrame` now expects a `mode` parameter to be present. If the `mode` parameter is missing, `restartFrame` errors out.
The various return values are deprecated and `callFrames` is always empty. Use the call frames from the `Debugger#paused` events instead, that fires once V8 pauses at the beginning of the restarted function.

member.summary: Resumes JavaScript execution.

member.summary: Makes backend skip steps in the script in blackboxed ranges. VM will try leave blacklisted scripts by performing 'step in' several times, finally resorting to 'step out' if unsuccessful. Positions array contains positions where blackbox state is changed. member.summary:
Edits JavaScript source live.
In general, functions that are currently on the stack can not be edited with a single exception: If the edited function is the top-most stack frame and that is the only activation of that function on the stack. In this case the live edit will be successful and a `Debugger.restartFrame` for the top-most function is automatically triggered.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandSettings
member.summary:
Restarts particular call frame from the beginning. The old, deprecated behavior of `restartFrame` is to stay paused and allow further CDP commands after a restart was scheduled. This can cause problems with restarting, so we now continue execution immediatly after it has been scheduled until we reach the beginning of the restarted frame.
To stay back-wards compatible, `restartFrame` now expects a `mode` parameter to be present. If the `mode` parameter is missing, `restartFrame` errors out.
The various return values are deprecated and `callFrames` is always empty. Use the call frames from the `Debugger#paused` events instead, that fires once V8 pauses at the beginning of the restarted function.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandSettings.CommandName
member.summary: Gets the name of the command.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandSettings.CallFrameId
member.summary: Call frame identifier to evaluate on.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandSettings.Mode
member.summary: The `mode` parameter must be present and set to 'StepInto', otherwise `restartFrame` will error out.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandResponse
member.summary:
Response for Restarts particular call frame from the beginning. The old, deprecated behavior of `restartFrame` is to stay paused and allow further CDP commands after a restart was scheduled. This can cause problems with restarting, so we now continue execution immediatly after it has been scheduled until we reach the beginning of the restarted frame.
To stay back-wards compatible, `restartFrame` now expects a `mode` parameter to be present. If the `mode` parameter is missing, `restartFrame` errors out.
The various return values are deprecated and `callFrames` is always empty. Use the call frames from the `Debugger#paused` events instead, that fires once V8 pauses at the beginning of the restarted function.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Debugger.SetScriptSourceCommandSettings
member.summary:
Edits JavaScript source live.
In general, functions that are currently on the stack can not be edited with a single exception: If the edited function is the top-most stack frame and that is the only activation of that function on the stack. In this case the live edit will be successful and a `Debugger.restartFrame` for the top-most function is automatically triggered.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Debugger.SetScriptSourceCommandSettings.CommandName
member.summary: Gets the name of the command.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Debugger.SetScriptSourceCommandSettings.ScriptId
member.summary: Id of the script to edit.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Debugger.SetScriptSourceCommandSettings.ScriptSource
member.summary: New content of the script.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Debugger.SetScriptSourceCommandSettings.DryRun
member.summary: If true the change will not actually be applied. Dry run may be used to get result description without actually modifying the code.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Debugger.SetScriptSourceCommandSettings.AllowTopFrameEditing
member.summary: If true, then `scriptSource` is allowed to change the function on top of the stack as long as the top-most stack frame is the only activation of that function.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Debugger.SetScriptSourceCommandResponse
member.summary:
Response for Edits JavaScript source live.
In general, functions that are currently on the stack can not be edited with a single exception: If the edited function is the top-most stack frame and that is the only activation of that function on the stack. In this case the live edit will be successful and a `Debugger.restartFrame` for the top-most function is automatically triggered.

member.summary: New stack trace in case editing has happened while VM was stopped.

member.summary: Whether current call stack was modified after applying the changes.

member.summary: Async stack trace, if any.

member.name: E:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Fetch.FetchAdapter.RequestPaused
member.summary: Issued when the domain is enabled and the request URL matches the specified filter. The request is paused until the client responds with one of continueRequest, failRequest or fulfillRequest. The stage of the request can be determined by presence of responseErrorReason and responseStatusCode -- the request is at the response stage if either of these fields is present and in the request stage otherwise. Redirect responses and subsequent requests are reported similarly to regular responses and requests. Redirect responses may be distinguished by the value of `responseStatusCode` (which is one of 301, 302, 303, 307, 308) along with presence of the `location` header. Requests resulting from a redirect will have `redirectedRequestId` field set.

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Fetch.FetchAdapter.GetResponseBody(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Fetch.GetResponseBodyCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Causes the body of the response to be received from the server and returned as a single string. May only be issued for a request that is paused in the Response stage and is mutually exclusive with takeResponseBodyForInterceptionAsStream. Calling other methods that affect the request or disabling fetch domain before body is received results in an undefined behavior. Note that the response body is not available for redirects. Requests paused in the _redirect received_ state may be differentiated by `responseCode` and presence of `location` response header, see comments to `requestPaused` for details.

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Fetch.FetchAdapter.TakeResponseBodyAsStream(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Fetch.TakeResponseBodyAsStreamCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Returns a handle to the stream representing the response body. The request must be paused in the HeadersReceived stage. Note that after this command the request can't be continued as is -- client either needs to cancel it or to provide the response body. The stream only supports sequential read, IO.read will fail if the position is specified. This method is mutually exclusive with getResponseBody. Calling other methods that affect the request or disabling fetch domain before body is received results in an undefined behavior.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.HeapProfiler.StartSamplingCommandSettings.IncludeObjectsCollectedByMajorGC
member.summary: By default, the sampling heap profiler reports only objects which are still alive when the profile is returned via getSamplingProfile or stopSampling, which is useful for determining what functions contribute the most to steady-state memory usage. This flag instructs the sampling heap profiler to also include information about objects discarded by major GC, which will show which functions cause large temporary memory usage or long GC pauses.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.HeapProfiler.StartSamplingCommandSettings.IncludeObjectsCollectedByMinorGC
member.summary: By default, the sampling heap profiler reports only objects which are still alive when the profile is returned via getSamplingProfile or stopSampling, which is useful for determining what functions contribute the most to steady-state memory usage. This flag instructs the sampling heap profiler to also include information about objects discarded by minor GC, which is useful when tuning a latency-sensitive application for minimal GC activity.

member.summary: Response to Network.requestIntercepted which either modifies the request to continue with any modifications, or blocks it, or completes it with the provided response bytes. If a network fetch occurs as a result which encounters a redirect an additional Network.requestIntercepted event will be sent with the same InterceptionId. Deprecated, use Fetch.continueRequest, Fetch.fulfillRequest and Fetch.failRequest instead.

member.summary: If set this causes the request to fail with the given reason. Passing `Aborted` for requests marked with `isNavigationRequest` also cancels the navigation. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.RawResponse
member.summary: If set the requests completes using with the provided base64 encoded raw response, including HTTP status line and headers etc... Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.Url
member.summary: If set the request url will be modified in a way that's not observable by page. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.summary: If set this allows the request method to be overridden. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.summary: If set this allows the request headers to be changed. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.summary: Response to a requestIntercepted with an authChallenge. Must not be set otherwise.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.PWA.ChangeAppUserSettingsCommandSettings
member.summary:
Changes user settings of the web app identified by its manifestId. If the app was not installed, this command returns an error. Unset parameters will be ignored; unrecognized values will cause an error.
Unlike the ones defined in the manifest files of the web apps, these settings are provided by the browser and controlled by the users, they impact the way the browser handling the web apps.
See the comment of each parameter.

member.summary: Gets or sets the manifestId

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.PWA.ChangeAppUserSettingsCommandSettings.LinkCapturing
member.summary:
If user allows the links clicked on by the user in the app's scope, or extended scope if the manifest has scope extensions and the flags `DesktopPWAsLinkCapturingWithScopeExtensions` and `WebAppEnableScopeExtensions` are enabled.
Note, the API does not support resetting the linkCapturing to the initial value, uninstalling and installing the web app again will reset it.
TODO(crbug.com/339453269): Setting this value on ChromeOS is not supported yet.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.PWA.InstallCommandSettings
member.summary:
Installs the given manifest identity, optionally using the given installUrlOrBundleUrl
IWA-specific install description: manifestId corresponds to isolated-app:// + web_package::SignedWebBundleId
File installation mode: The installUrlOrBundleUrl can be either file:// or http(s):// pointing to a signed web bundle (.swbn). In this case SignedWebBundleId must correspond to The .swbn file's signing key.
Dev proxy installation mode: installUrlOrBundleUrl must be http(s):// that serves dev mode IWA. web_package::SignedWebBundleId must be of type dev proxy.
The advantage of dev proxy mode is that all changes to IWA automatically will be reflected in the running app without reinstallation.
To generate bundle id for proxy mode: 1. Generate 32 random bytes. 2. Add a specific suffix at the end following the documentation https://github.com/WICG/isolated-web-apps/blob/main/Scheme.md#suffix 3. Encode the entire sequence using Base32 without padding.
If Chrome is not in IWA dev mode, the installation will fail, regardless of the state of the allowlist.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.PWA.LaunchFilesInAppCommandSettings
member.summary:
Opens one or more local files from an installed web app identified by its manifestId. The web app needs to have file handlers registered to process the files. The API returns one or more page Target.TargetIDs which can be used to attach to via Target.attachToTarget or similar APIs. If some files in the parameters cannot be handled by the web app, they will be ignored. If none of the files can be handled, this API returns an error. If no files are provided as the parameter, this API also returns an error.
According to the definition of the file handlers in the manifest file, one Target.TargetID may represent a page handling one or more files. The order of the returned Target.TargetIDs is not guaranteed.
TODO(crbug.com/339454034): Check the existences of the input files.

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.PWA.PWAAdapter.ChangeAppUserSettings(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.PWA.ChangeAppUserSettingsCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary:
Changes user settings of the web app identified by its manifestId. If the app was not installed, this command returns an error. Unset parameters will be ignored; unrecognized values will cause an error.
Unlike the ones defined in the manifest files of the web apps, these settings are provided by the browser and controlled by the users, they impact the way the browser handling the web apps.
See the comment of each parameter.

member.summary: Gets the name of the command.

member.summary: Paper orientation. Defaults to false.

member.summary: Display header and footer. Defaults to false.

member.summary: Print background graphics. Defaults to false.

member.summary: Scale of the webpage rendering. Defaults to 1.

member.summary: Paper width in inches. Defaults to 8.5 inches.

member.summary: Paper height in inches. Defaults to 11 inches.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.MarginTop
member.summary: Top margin in inches. Defaults to 1cm (~0.4 inches).

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.MarginBottom
member.summary: Bottom margin in inches. Defaults to 1cm (~0.4 inches).

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.MarginLeft
member.summary: Left margin in inches. Defaults to 1cm (~0.4 inches).

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.MarginRight
member.summary: Right margin in inches. Defaults to 1cm (~0.4 inches).

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.PageRanges
member.summary: Paper ranges to print, one based, e.g., '1-5, 8, 11-13'. Pages are printed in the document order, not in the order specified, and no more than once. Defaults to empty string, which implies the entire document is printed. The page numbers are quietly capped to actual page count of the document, and ranges beyond the end of the document are ignored. If this results in no pages to print, an error is reported. It is an error to specify a range with start greater than end.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.HeaderTemplate
member.summary: HTML template for the print header. Should be valid HTML markup with following classes used to inject printing values into them: - `date`: formatted print date - `title`: document title - `url`: document location - `pageNumber`: current page number - `totalPages`: total pages in the document For example, `` would generate span containing the title.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.FooterTemplate
member.summary: HTML template for the print footer. Should use the same format as the `headerTemplate`.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.PreferCSSPageSize
member.summary: Whether or not to prefer page size as defined by css. Defaults to false, in which case the content will be scaled to fit the paper size.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.TransferMode
member.summary: return as stream

member.summary: Whether or not to generate tagged (accessible) PDF. Defaults to embedder choice.

member.summary: Whether or not to embed the document outline into the PDF.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Page.ProduceCompilationCacheCommandSettings
member.summary: Requests backend to produce compilation cache for the specified scripts. `scripts` are appended to the list of scripts for which the cache would be produced. The list may be reset during page navigation. When script with a matching URL is encountered, the cache is optionally produced upon backend discretion, based on internal heuristics. member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Preload.RuleSet.SourceText
member.summary:
Source text of JSON representing the rule set. If it comes from `script` tag, it is the textContent of the node. Note that it is a JSON for valid case.
See also: - https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/speculation-rules.html - https://github.com/WICG/nav-speculation/blob/main/triggers.md

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Preload.RuleSet.BackendNodeId
member.summary:
A speculation rule set is either added through an inline `script` tag or through an external resource via the 'Speculation-Rules' HTTP header. For the first case, we include the BackendNodeId of the relevant `script` tag. For the second case, we include the external URL where the rule set was loaded from, and also RequestId if Network domain is enabled.
See also: - https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/speculation-rules.html#speculation-rules-script - https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/speculation-rules.html#speculation-rules-header

member.summary: Gets or sets the name

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Runtime.AddBindingCommandSettings.ExecutionContextId
member.summary: If specified, the binding would only be exposed to the specified execution context. If omitted and `executionContextName` is not set, the binding is exposed to all execution contexts of the target. This parameter is mutually exclusive with `executionContextName`. Deprecated in favor of `executionContextName` due to an unclear use case and bugs in implementation (crbug.com/1169639). `executionContextId` will be removed in the future.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Runtime.AddBindingCommandSettings.ExecutionContextName
member.summary: If specified, the binding is exposed to the executionContext with matching name, even for contexts created after the binding is added. See also `ExecutionContext.name` and `worldName` parameter to `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument`. This parameter is mutually exclusive with `executionContextId`.

member.summary: Terminate execution after timing out (number of milliseconds).

member.summary: Disable breakpoints during execution.

member.summary: Setting this flag to true enables `let` re-declaration and top-level `await`. Note that `let` variables can only be re-declared if they originate from `replMode` themselves.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.AllowUnsafeEvalBlockedByCSP
member.summary: The Content Security Policy (CSP) for the target might block 'unsafe-eval' which includes eval(), Function(), setTimeout() and setInterval() when called with non-callable arguments. This flag bypasses CSP for this evaluation and allows unsafe-eval. Defaults to true.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.UniqueContextId
member.summary: An alternative way to specify the execution context to evaluate in. Compared to contextId that may be reused across processes, this is guaranteed to be system-unique, so it can be used to prevent accidental evaluation of the expression in context different than intended (e.g. as a result of navigation across process boundaries). This is mutually exclusive with `contextId`.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Target.CreateTargetCommandSettings.Focus
member.summary: If specified, the option is used to determine if the new target should be focused or not. By default, the focus behavior depends on the value of the background field. For example, background=false and focus=false will result in the target tab being opened but the browser window remain unchanged (if it was in the background, it will remain in the background) and background=false with focus=undefined will result in the window being focused. Using background: true and focus: true is not supported and will result in an error.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V148.Target.SetAutoAttachCommandSettings
member.summary: Controls whether to automatically attach to new targets which are considered to be directly related to this one (for example, iframes or workers). When turned on, attaches to all existing related targets as well. When turned off, automatically detaches from all currently attached targets. This also clears all targets added by `autoAttachRelated` from the list of targets to watch for creation of related targets. You might want to call this recursively for auto-attached targets to attach to all available targets.

member.summary: Query a DOM node's accessibility subtree for accessible name and role. This command computes the name and role for all nodes in the subtree, including those that are ignored for accessibility, and returns those that match the specified name and role. If no DOM node is specified, or the DOM node does not exist, the command returns an error. If neither `accessibleName` or `role` is specified, it returns all the accessibility nodes in the subtree.

Address UI is a two dimensional array, each inner array is an "address information line", and when rendered in a UI surface should be displayed as such. member.summary: Resolve the specified values in the context of the provided element. For example, a value of '1em' is evaluated according to the computed 'font-size' of the element and a value 'calc(1px + 2px)' will be resolved to '3px'. If the `propertyName` was specified the `values` are resolved as if they were property's declaration. If a value cannot be parsed according to the provided property syntax, the value is parsed using combined syntax as if null `propertyName` was provided. If the value cannot be resolved even then, return the provided value without any changes. Note: this function currently does not resolve CSS random() function, it returns unmodified random() function parts.`

member.summary: Starts tracking the given computed styles for updates. The specified array of properties replaces the one previously specified. Pass empty array to disable tracking. Use takeComputedStyleUpdates to retrieve the list of nodes that had properties modified. The changes to computed style properties are only tracked for nodes pushed to the front-end by the DOM agent. If no changes to the tracked properties occur after the node has been pushed to the front-end, no updates will be issued for the node.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.CSS.ResolveValuesCommandSettings
member.summary: Resolve the specified values in the context of the provided element. For example, a value of '1em' is evaluated according to the computed 'font-size' of the element and a value 'calc(1px + 2px)' will be resolved to '3px'. If the `propertyName` was specified the `values` are resolved as if they were property's declaration. If a value cannot be parsed according to the provided property syntax, the value is parsed using combined syntax as if null `propertyName` was provided. If the value cannot be resolved even then, return the provided value without any changes. Note: this function currently does not resolve CSS random() function, it returns unmodified random() function parts.`

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.CSS.TrackComputedStyleUpdatesCommandSettings
member.summary: Starts tracking the given computed styles for updates. The specified array of properties replaces the one previously specified. Pass empty array to disable tracking. Use takeComputedStyleUpdates to retrieve the list of nodes that had properties modified. The changes to computed style properties are only tracked for nodes pushed to the front-end by the DOM agent. If no changes to the tracked properties occur after the node has been pushed to the front-end, no updates will be issued for the node.

member.summary: Starts tracking the given node for the computed style updates and whenever the computed style is updated for node, it queues a `computedStyleUpdated` event with throttling. member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Debugger.DebuggerAdapter.RestartFrame(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary:
Restarts particular call frame from the beginning. The old, deprecated behavior of `restartFrame` is to stay paused and allow further CDP commands after a restart was scheduled. This can cause problems with restarting, so we now continue execution immediatly after it has been scheduled until we reach the beginning of the restarted frame.
To stay back-wards compatible, `restartFrame` now expects a `mode` parameter to be present. If the `mode` parameter is missing, `restartFrame` errors out.
The various return values are deprecated and `callFrames` is always empty. Use the call frames from the `Debugger#paused` events instead, that fires once V8 pauses at the beginning of the restarted function.

member.summary: Resumes JavaScript execution.

member.summary:
Edits JavaScript source live.
In general, functions that are currently on the stack can not be edited with a single exception: If the edited function is the top-most stack frame and that is the only activation of that function on the stack. member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandSettings
member.summary:
Restarts particular call frame from the beginning. The old, deprecated behavior of `restartFrame` is to stay paused and allow further CDP commands after a restart was scheduled. This can cause problems with restarting, so we now continue execution immediatly after it has been scheduled until we reach the beginning of the restarted frame.
To stay back-wards compatible, `restartFrame` now expects a `mode` parameter to be present. If the `mode` parameter is missing, `restartFrame` errors out.
The various return values are deprecated and `callFrames` is always empty. Use the call frames from the `Debugger#paused` events instead, that fires once V8 pauses at the beginning of the restarted function.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandSettings.CommandName
member.summary: Gets the name of the command.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandSettings.CallFrameId
member.summary: Call frame identifier to evaluate on.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandSettings.Mode
member.summary: The `mode` parameter must be present and set to 'StepInto', otherwise `restartFrame` will error out.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandResponse
member.summary:
Response for Restarts particular call frame from the beginning. The old, deprecated behavior of `restartFrame` is to stay paused and allow further CDP commands after a restart was scheduled. This can cause problems with restarting, so we now continue execution immediatly after it has been scheduled until we reach the beginning of the restarted frame.
To stay back-wards compatible, `restartFrame` now expects a `mode` parameter to be present. If the `mode` parameter is missing, `restartFrame` errors out.
The various return values are deprecated and `callFrames` is always empty. Use the call frames from the `Debugger#paused` events instead, that fires once V8 pauses at the beginning of the restarted function.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Debugger.SetScriptSourceCommandSettings
member.summary:
Edits JavaScript source live.
In general, functions that are currently on the stack can not be edited with a single exception: If the edited function is the top-most stack frame and that is the only activation of that function on the stack. In this case the live edit will be successful and a `Debugger.restartFrame` for the top-most function is automatically triggered.

member.name: E:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Fetch.FetchAdapter.RequestPaused
member.summary: Issued when the domain is enabled and the request URL matches the specified filter. The request is paused until the client responds with one of continueRequest, failRequest or fulfillRequest. The stage of the request can be determined by presence of responseErrorReason and responseStatusCode -- the request is at the response stage if either of these fields is present and in the request stage otherwise. Redirect responses and subsequent requests are reported similarly to regular responses and requests. Redirect responses may be distinguished by the value of `responseStatusCode` (which is one of 301, 302, 303, 307, 308) along with presence of the `location` header. Requests resulting from a redirect will have `redirectedRequestId` field set.

member.name: E:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Fetch.FetchAdapter.AuthRequired
member.summary: Issued when the domain is enabled with handleAuthRequests set to true. The request is paused until client responds with continueWithAuth.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Fetch.RequestPausedEventArgs
member.summary: Issued when the domain is enabled and the request URL matches the specified filter. The request is paused until the client responds with one of continueRequest, failRequest or fulfillRequest. The stage of the request can be determined by presence of responseErrorReason and responseStatusCode -- the request is at the response stage if either of these fields is present and in the request stage otherwise. Redirect responses and subsequent requests are reported similarly to regular responses and requests. Redirect responses may be distinguished by the value of `responseStatusCode` (which is one of 301, 302, 303, 307, 308) along with presence of the `location` header. Requests resulting from a redirect will have `redirectedRequestId` field set.

member.summary: Maximum stack depth. The default value is 128.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.HeapProfiler.StartSamplingCommandSettings.IncludeObjectsCollectedByMajorGC
member.summary: By default, the sampling heap profiler reports only objects which are still alive when the profile is returned via getSamplingProfile or stopSampling, which is useful for determining what functions contribute the most to steady-state memory usage. This flag instructs the sampling heap profiler to also include information about objects discarded by major GC, which will show which functions cause large temporary memory usage or long GC pauses.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.HeapProfiler.StartSamplingCommandSettings.IncludeObjectsCollectedByMinorGC
member.summary: By default, the sampling heap profiler reports only objects which are still alive when the profile is returned via getSamplingProfile or stopSampling, which is useful for determining what functions contribute the most to steady-state memory usage. This flag instructs the sampling heap profiler to also include information about objects discarded by minor GC, which is useful when tuning a latency-sensitive application for minimal GC activity.

member.summary: Keep in sync with MediaLogMessageLevel We are currently keeping the message level 'error' separate from the PlayerError type because right now they represent different things, this one being a DVLOG(ERROR) style log message that gets printed based on what log level is selected in the UI, and the other is a representation of a media::PipelineStatus object. Soon however we're going to be moving away from using PipelineStatus for errors and introducing a new error type which should hopefully let us integrate the error log level into the PlayerError type.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Network.AdProvenance
member.summary: Represents the provenance of an ad resource or element. Only one of `filterlistRule` or `adScriptAncestry` can be set. If `filterlistRule` is provided, the resource URL directly matches a filter list rule. If `adScriptAncestry` is provided, an ad script initiated the resource fetch or appended the element to the DOM. If neither is provided, the entity is known to be an ad, but provenance tracking information is unavailable.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings
member.summary: Response to Network.requestIntercepted which either modifies the request to continue with any modifications, or blocks it, or completes it with the provided response bytes. If a network fetch occurs as a result which encounters a redirect an additional Network.requestIntercepted event will be sent with the same InterceptionId. Deprecated, use Fetch.continueRequest, Fetch.fulfillRequest and Fetch.failRequest instead.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.CommandName
member.summary: Gets the name of the command.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.InterceptionId
member.summary: Gets or sets the interceptionId

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.ErrorReason
member.summary: If set this causes the request to fail with the given reason. Passing `Aborted` for requests marked with `isNavigationRequest` also cancels the navigation. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.RawResponse
member.summary: If set the requests completes using with the provided base64 encoded raw response, including HTTP status line and headers etc... Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.Url
member.summary: If set the request url will be modified in a way that's not observable by page. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.Method
member.summary: If set this allows the request method to be overridden. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.PostData
member.summary: If set this allows postData to be set. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.Headers
member.summary: If set this allows the request headers to be changed. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.AuthChallengeResponse
member.summary: Response to a requestIntercepted with an authChallenge. Must not be set otherwise.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandResponse
member.summary: Response for Response to Network.requestIntercepted which either modifies the request to continue with any modifications, or blocks it, or completes it with the provided response bytes. If a network fetch occurs as a result which encounters a redirect an additional Network.requestIntercepted event will be sent with the same InterceptionId. Deprecated, use Fetch.continueRequest, Fetch.fulfillRequest and Fetch.failRequest instead.

member.summary: Returns a handle to the stream representing the response body. member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.PWA.ChangeAppUserSettingsCommandSettings
member.summary:
Changes user settings of the web app identified by its manifestId. If the app was not installed, this command returns an error. Unset parameters will be ignored; unrecognized values will cause an error.
Unlike the ones defined in the manifest files of the web apps, these settings are provided by the browser and controlled by the users, they impact the way the browser handling the web apps.
See the comment of each parameter.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.PWA.InstallCommandSettings
member.summary:
Installs the given manifest identity, optionally using the given installUrlOrBundleUrl
IWA-specific install description: manifestId corresponds to isolated-app:// + web_package::SignedWebBundleId
File installation mode: The installUrlOrBundleUrl can be either file:// or http(s):// pointing to a signed web bundle (.swbn). In this case SignedWebBundleId must correspond to The .swbn file's signing key.
Dev proxy installation mode: installUrlOrBundleUrl must be http(s):// that serves dev mode IWA. web_package::SignedWebBundleId must be of type dev proxy.
The advantage of dev proxy mode is that all changes to IWA automatically will be reflected in the running app without reinstallation.
To generate bundle id for proxy mode: 1. Generate 32 random bytes. 2. Add a specific suffix at the end following the documentation https://github.com/WICG/isolated-web-apps/blob/main/Scheme.md#suffix 3. Encode the entire sequence using Base32 without padding.
If Chrome is not in IWA dev mode, the installation will fail, regardless of the state of the allowlist.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.PWA.LaunchFilesInAppCommandSettings
member.summary:
Opens one or more local files from an installed web app identified by its manifestId. The web app needs to have file handlers registered to process the files. The API returns one or more page Target.TargetIDs which can be used to attach to via Target.attachToTarget or similar APIs. If some files in the parameters cannot be handled by the web app, they will be ignored. If none of the files can be handled, this API returns an error. If no files are provided as the parameter, this API also returns an error.
According to the definition of the file handlers in the manifest file, one Target.TargetID may represent a page handling one or more files. The order of the returned Target.TargetIDs is not guaranteed.
TODO(crbug.com/339454034): Check the existences of the input files.

To generate bundle id for proxy mode: 1. Generate 32 random bytes. 2. Add a specific suffix at the end following the documentation https://github.com/WICG/isolated-web-apps/blob/main/Scheme.md#suffix 3. Encode the entire sequence using Base32 without padding.
If Chrome is not in IWA dev mode, the installation will fail, regardless of the state of the allowlist.

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.PWA.PWAAdapter.Launch(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.PWA.LaunchCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Launches the installed web app, or an url in the same web app instead of the default start url if it is provided. Returns a page Target.TargetID which can be used to attach to via Target.attachToTarget or similar APIs.

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.PWA.PWAAdapter.LaunchFilesInApp(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.PWA.LaunchFilesInAppCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary:
Opens one or more local files from an installed web app identified by its manifestId. The web app needs to have file handlers registered to process the files. The API returns one or more page Target.TargetIDs which can be used to attach to via Target.attachToTarget or similar APIs. If some files in the parameters cannot be handled by the web app, they will be ignored. If none of the files can be handled, this API returns an error. If no files are provided as the parameter, this API also returns an error.
According to the definition of the file handlers in the manifest file, one Target.TargetID may represent a page handling one or more files. The order of the returned Target.TargetIDs is not guaranteed.
TODO(crbug.com/339454034): Check the existences of the input files.

member.summary: Opens the current page in its web app identified by the manifest id, needs to be called on a page target. This function returns immediately without waiting for the app to finish loading.

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.PWA.PWAAdapter.ChangeAppUserSettings(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.PWA.ChangeAppUserSettingsCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary:
Changes user settings of the web app identified by its manifestId. If the app was not installed, this command returns an error. Unset parameters will be ignored; unrecognized values will cause an error.
Unlike the ones defined in the manifest files of the web apps, these settings are provided by the browser and controlled by the users, they impact the way the browser handling the web apps.
See the comment of each parameter.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.PageRanges
member.summary: Paper ranges to print, one based, e.g., '1-5, 8, 11-13'. Pages are printed in the document order, not in the order specified, and no more than once. Defaults to empty string, which implies the entire document is printed. The page numbers are quietly capped to actual page count of the document, and ranges beyond the end of the document are ignored. If this results in no pages to print, an error is reported. It is an error to specify a range with start greater than end.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.HeaderTemplate
member.summary: HTML template for the print header. Should be valid HTML markup with following classes used to inject printing values into them: - `date`: formatted print date - `title`: document title - `url`: document location - `pageNumber`: current page number - `totalPages`: total pages in the document For example, `` would generate span containing the title.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.FooterTemplate
member.summary: HTML template for the print footer. Should use the same format as the `headerTemplate`.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.PreferCSSPageSize
member.summary: Whether or not to prefer page size as defined by css. Defaults to false, in which case the content will be scaled to fit the paper size.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Preload.RuleSet.SourceText
member.summary:
Source text of JSON representing the rule set. If it comes from `script` tag, it is the textContent of the node. Note that it is a JSON for valid case.
See also: - https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/speculation-rules.html - https://github.com/WICG/nav-speculation/blob/main/triggers.md

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Preload.RuleSet.BackendNodeId
member.summary:
A speculation rule set is either added through an inline `script` tag or through an external resource via the 'Speculation-Rules' HTTP header. For the first case, we include the BackendNodeId of the relevant `script` tag. For the second case, we include the external URL where the rule set was loaded from, and also RequestId if Network domain is enabled.
See also: - https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/speculation-rules.html#speculation-rules-script - https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/speculation-rules.html#speculation-rules-header

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Runtime.AddBindingCommandSettings
member.summary: If executionContextId is empty, adds binding with the given name on the global objects of all inspected contexts, including those created later, bindings survive reloads. Binding function takes exactly one argument, this argument should be string, in case of any other input, function throws an exception. Each binding function call produces Runtime.bindingCalled notification.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Runtime.AddBindingCommandSettings.CommandName
member.summary: Gets the name of the command.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Runtime.AddBindingCommandSettings.Name
member.summary: Gets or sets the name

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Runtime.AddBindingCommandSettings.ExecutionContextId
member.summary: If specified, the binding would only be exposed to the specified execution context. If omitted and `executionContextName` is not set, the binding is exposed to all execution contexts of the target. This parameter is mutually exclusive with `executionContextName`. Deprecated in favor of `executionContextName` due to an unclear use case and bugs in implementation (crbug.com/1169639). `executionContextId` will be removed in the future.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Runtime.AddBindingCommandSettings.ExecutionContextName
member.summary: If specified, the binding is exposed to the executionContext with matching name, even for contexts created after the binding is added. See also `ExecutionContext.name` and `worldName` parameter to `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument`. This parameter is mutually exclusive with `executionContextId`.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Runtime.AddBindingCommandResponse
member.summary: Response for If executionContextId is empty, adds binding with the given name on the global objects of all inspected contexts, including those created later, bindings survive reloads. Binding function takes exactly one argument, this argument should be string, in case of any other input, function throws an exception. Each binding function call produces Runtime.bindingCalled notification.

member.summary: Specifies in which execution context to perform evaluation. If the parameter is omitted the evaluation will be performed in the context of the inspected page. This is mutually exclusive with `uniqueContextId`, which offers an alternative way to identify the execution context that is more reliable in a multi-process environment.

member.summary: Whether the result is expected to be a JSON object that should be sent by value.

member.summary: Whether preview should be generated for the result.

member.summary: Whether execution should be treated as initiated by user in the UI.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.AwaitPromise
member.summary: Whether execution should `await` for resulting value and return once awaited promise is resolved.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.ThrowOnSideEffect
member.summary: Whether to throw an exception if side effect cannot be ruled out during evaluation. This implies `disableBreaks` below.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.Timeout
member.summary: Terminate execution after timing out (number of milliseconds).

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.DisableBreaks
member.summary: Disable breakpoints during execution.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.ReplMode
member.summary: Setting this flag to true enables `let` re-declaration and top-level `await`. Note that `let` variables can only be re-declared if they originate from `replMode` themselves.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.AllowUnsafeEvalBlockedByCSP
member.summary: The Content Security Policy (CSP) for the target might block 'unsafe-eval' which includes eval(), Function(), setTimeout() and setInterval() when called with non-callable arguments. This flag bypasses CSP for this evaluation and allows unsafe-eval. Defaults to true.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.UniqueContextId
member.summary: An alternative way to specify the execution context to evaluate in. Compared to contextId that may be reused across processes, this is guaranteed to be system-unique, so it can be used to prevent accidental evaluation of the expression in context different than intended (e.g. as a result of navigation across process boundaries). This is mutually exclusive with `contextId`.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.SerializationOptions
member.summary: Specifies the result serialization. If provided, overrides `generatePreview` and `returnByValue`.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Target.CreateTargetCommandSettings.Hidden
member.summary: Whether to create a hidden target. The hidden target is observable via protocol, but not present in the tab UI strip. Cannot be created with `forTab: true`, `newWindow: true` or `background: false`. The life-time of the tab is limited to the life-time of the session.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Target.CreateTargetCommandSettings.Focus
member.summary: If specified, the option is used to determine if the new target should be focused or not. By default, the focus behavior depends on the value of the background field. For example, background=false and focus=false will result in the target tab being opened but the browser window remain unchanged (if it was in the background, it will remain in the background) and background=false with focus=undefined will result in the window being focused. Using background: true and focus: true is not supported and will result in an error.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Target.ExposeDevToolsProtocolCommandSettings
member.summary:
Inject object to the target's main frame that provides a communication channel with browser target.
Injected object will be available as `window[bindingName]`.
The object has the following API: - `binding.send(json)` - a method to send messages over the remote debugging protocol - `binding.onmessage = json => handleMessage(json)` - a callback that will be called for the protocol notifications and command responses.

member.summary: Binding name, 'cdp' if not specified.

member.summary: If true, inherits the current root session's permissions (default: false).

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Target.ExposeDevToolsProtocolCommandResponse
member.summary:
Response for Inject object to the target's main frame that provides a communication channel with browser target.
Injected object will be available as `window[bindingName]`.
The object has the following API: - `binding.send(json)` - a method to send messages over the remote debugging protocol - `binding.onmessage = json => handleMessage(json)` - a callback that will be called for the protocol notifications and command responses.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V149.Target.SetAutoAttachCommandSettings
member.summary: Controls whether to automatically attach to new targets which are considered to be directly related to this one (for example, iframes or workers). When turned on, attaches to all existing related targets as well. When turned off, automatically detaches from all currently attached targets. This also clears all targets added by `autoAttachRelated` from the list of targets to watch for creation of related targets. You might want to call this recursively for auto-attached targets to attach to all available targets.

member.summary:
Inject object to the target's main frame that provides a communication channel with browser target.
Injected object will be available as `window[bindingName]`.
The object has the following API: - `binding.send(json)` - a method to send messages over the remote debugging protocol - `binding.onmessage = json => handleMessage(json)` - a callback that will be called for the protocol notifications and command responses.

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V150.Accessibility.AccessibilityAdapter.QueryAXTree(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V150.Accessibility.QueryAXTreeCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Query a DOM node's accessibility subtree for accessible name and role. This command computes the name and role for all nodes in the subtree, including those that are ignored for accessibility, and returns those that match the specified name and role. If no DOM node is specified, or the DOM node does not exist, the command returns an error. If neither `accessibleName` or `role` is specified, it returns all the accessibility nodes in the subtree.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V150.Accessibility.QueryAXTreeCommandSettings
member.summary: Query a DOM node's accessibility subtree for accessible name and role. This command computes the name and role for all nodes in the subtree, including those that are ignored for accessibility, and returns those that match the specified name and role. If no DOM node is specified, or the DOM node does not exist, the command returns an error. If neither `accessibleName` or `role` is specified, it returns all the accessibility nodes in the subtree.

member.summary: Find nodes with this computed name.

If no DOM node is specified, or the DOM node does not exist, the command returns an error. If neither `accessibleName` or `role` is specified, it returns all the accessibility nodes in the subtree.

member.summary: Defines how an address can be displayed like in chrome://settings/addresses. Address UI is a two dimensional array, each inner array is an "address information line", and when rendered in a UI surface should be displayed as such. The following address UI for instance: [[{name: "GIVE_NAME", value: "Jon"}, {name: "FAMILY_NAME", value: "Doe"}], [{name: "CITY", value: "Munich"}, {name: "ZIP", value: "81456"}]] should allow the receiver to render: Jon Doe Munich 81456

member.summary: Resolve the specified values in the context of the provided element. For example, a value of '1em' is evaluated according to the computed 'font-size' of the element and a value 'calc(1px + 2px)' will be resolved to '3px'. If the `propertyName` was specified the `values` are resolved as if they were property's declaration. If a value cannot be parsed according to the provided property syntax, the value is parsed using combined syntax as if null `propertyName` was provided. If the value cannot be resolved even then, return the provided value without any changes. Note: this function currently does not resolve CSS random() function, it returns unmodified random() function parts.`

member.summary: Starts tracking the given node for the computed style updates and whenever the computed style is updated for node, it queues a `computedStyleUpdated` event with throttling. member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V150.CSS.CSSAdapter.TrackComputedStyleUpdates(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V150.CSS.TrackComputedStyleUpdatesCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Starts tracking the given computed styles for updates. The specified array of properties replaces the one previously specified. Pass empty array to disable tracking. Use takeComputedStyleUpdates to retrieve the list of nodes that had properties modified. The changes to computed style properties are only tracked for nodes pushed to the front-end by the DOM agent. If no changes to the tracked properties occur after the node has been pushed to the front-end, no updates will be issued for the node.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V150.CSS.ResolveValuesCommandSettings
member.summary: Resolve the specified values in the context of the provided element. For example, a value of '1em' is evaluated according to the computed 'font-size' of the element and a value 'calc(1px + 2px)' will be resolved to '3px'. If the `propertyName` was specified the `values` are resolved as if they were property's declaration. If a value cannot be parsed according to the provided property syntax, the value is parsed using combined syntax as if null `propertyName` was provided. If the value cannot be resolved even then, return the provided value without any changes. Note: this function currently does not resolve CSS random() function, it returns unmodified random() function parts.`

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V150.CSS.TrackComputedStyleUpdatesCommandSettings
member.summary: Starts tracking the given computed styles for updates. The specified array of properties replaces the one previously specified. Pass empty array to disable tracking. Use takeComputedStyleUpdates to retrieve the list of nodes that had properties modified. The changes to computed style properties are only tracked for nodes pushed to the front-end by the DOM agent. If no changes to the tracked properties occur after the node has been pushed to the front-end, no updates will be issued for the node.

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V150.Debugger.DebuggerAdapter.RestartFrame(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V150.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary:
Restarts particular call frame from the beginning. The old, deprecated behavior of `restartFrame` is to stay paused and allow further CDP commands after a restart was scheduled. This can cause problems with restarting, so we now continue execution immediatly after it has been scheduled until we reach the beginning of the restarted frame.
To stay back-wards compatible, `restartFrame` now expects a `mode` parameter to be present. If the `mode` parameter is missing, `restartFrame` errors out.
The various return values are deprecated and `callFrames` is always empty. Use the call frames from the `Debugger#paused` events instead, that fires once V8 pauses at the beginning of the restarted function.

member.summary: Resumes JavaScript execution.

member.summary: Makes backend skip steps in the script in blackboxed ranges. VM will try leave blacklisted scripts by performing 'step in' several times, finally resorting to 'step out' if unsuccessful. Positions array contains positions where blackbox state is changed. member.summary:
Edits JavaScript source live.
In general, functions that are currently on the stack can not be edited with a single exception: If the edited function is the top-most stack frame and that is the only activation of that function on the stack. In this case the live edit will be successful and a `Debugger.restartFrame` for the top-most function is automatically triggered.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V150.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandSettings
member.summary:
Restarts particular call frame from the beginning. The old, deprecated behavior of `restartFrame` is to stay paused and allow further CDP commands after a restart was scheduled. This can cause problems with restarting, so we now continue execution immediatly after it has been scheduled until we reach the beginning of the restarted frame.
To stay back-wards compatible, `restartFrame` now expects a `mode` parameter to be present. If the `mode` parameter is missing, `restartFrame` errors out.
The various return values are deprecated and `callFrames` is always empty. Use the call frames from the `Debugger#paused` events instead, that fires once V8 pauses at the beginning of the restarted function.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V150.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandSettings.CommandName
member.summary: Gets the name of the command.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V150.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandSettings.CallFrameId
member.summary: Call frame identifier to evaluate on.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V150.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandSettings.Mode
member.summary: The `mode` parameter must be present and set to 'StepInto', otherwise `restartFrame` will error out.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V150.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandResponse
member.summary:
Response for Restarts particular call frame from the beginning. The old, deprecated behavior of `restartFrame` is to stay paused and allow further CDP commands after a restart was scheduled. This can cause problems with restarting, so we now continue execution immediatly after it has been scheduled until we reach the beginning of the restarted frame.
To stay back-wards compatible, `restartFrame` now expects a `mode` parameter to be present. If the `mode` parameter is missing, `restartFrame` errors out.
The various return values are deprecated and `callFrames` is always empty. Use the call frames from the `Debugger#paused` events instead, that fires once V8 pauses at the beginning of the restarted function.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V150.Debugger.SetScriptSourceCommandSettings
member.summary:
Edits JavaScript source live.
In general, functions that are currently on the stack can not be edited with a single exception: If the edited function is the top-most stack frame and that is the only activation of that function on the stack. In this case the live edit will be successful and a `Debugger.restartFrame` for the top-most function is automatically triggered.

member.summary: Gets the name of the command.

member.summary: Id of the script to edit.

member.summary: New content of the script.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V150.Debugger.SetScriptSourceCommandSettings.DryRun
member.summary: If true the change will not actually be applied. Dry run may be used to get result description without actually modifying the code.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V150.Debugger.SetScriptSourceCommandSettings.AllowTopFrameEditing
member.summary: If true, then `scriptSource` is allowed to change the function on top of the stack as long as the top-most stack frame is the only activation of that function.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V150.Debugger.SetScriptSourceCommandResponse
member.summary:
Response for Edits JavaScript source live.
In general, functions that are currently on the stack can not be edited with a single exception: If the edited function is the top-most stack frame and that is the only activation of that function on the stack. In this case the live edit will be successful and a `Debugger.restartFrame` for the top-most function is automatically triggered.

member.name: E:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V150.Fetch.FetchAdapter.RequestPaused
member.summary: Issued when the domain is enabled and the request URL matches the specified filter. The request is paused until the client responds with one of continueRequest, failRequest or fulfillRequest. The stage of the request can be determined by presence of responseErrorReason and responseStatusCode -- the request is at the response stage if either of these fields is present and in the request stage otherwise. Redirect responses and subsequent requests are reported similarly to regular responses and requests. Redirect responses may be distinguished by the value of `responseStatusCode` (which is one of 301, 302, 303, 307, 308) along with presence of the `location` header. Requests resulting from a redirect will have `redirectedRequestId` field set.

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V150.Fetch.FetchAdapter.GetResponseBody(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V150.Fetch.GetResponseBodyCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Causes the body of the response to be received from the server and returned as a single string. May only be issued for a request that is paused in the Response stage and is mutually exclusive with takeResponseBodyForInterceptionAsStream. Calling other methods that affect the request or disabling fetch domain before body is received results in an undefined behavior. Note that the response body is not available for redirects. Requests paused in the _redirect received_ state may be differentiated by `responseCode` and presence of `location` response header, see comments to `requestPaused` for details.

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V150.Fetch.FetchAdapter.TakeResponseBodyAsStream(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V150.Fetch.TakeResponseBodyAsStreamCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Returns a handle to the stream representing the response body. The request must be paused in the HeadersReceived stage. Note that after this command the request can't be continued as is -- client either needs to cancel it or to provide the response body. The stream only supports sequential read, IO.read will fail if the position is specified. This method is mutually exclusive with getResponseBody. Calling other methods that affect the request or disabling fetch domain before body is received results in an undefined behavior.

member.summary: The interval between BeginFrames that is reported to the compositor, in milliseconds. Defaults to a 60 frames/second interval, i.e. about 16.666 milliseconds.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V150.HeadlessExperimental.BeginFrameCommandSettings.NoDisplayUpdates
member.summary: Whether updates should not be committed and drawn onto the display. False by default. If true, only side effects of the BeginFrame will be run, such as layout and animations, but any visual updates may not be visible on the display or in screenshots.
